_about: Thresholds for artcolour.py (the colour and look tool) and the look lines artjudge.py and artblock.py take from it. Tune here, not in code; say why in the commit. Calibration notes: build/reports/art-retrospective-2026-11-06.md.

house._about: The house family (build/reports/s17-palette-review.md): Wada combinations 283 (the sage and maroon), 249 and 311 (maroon, ecru stone, ochre gold, honey), 200 (Chromium Green with Carmine Red again), and the single colours that review matched our fixed set to.

colour._about: Main colours: k-means in CIE Lab (D65) on the opaque pixels; distances are CIEDE2000 with kL (lightness weight) 2, so a tint or shade of a Wada colour counts as near (the review read the stone and marble as tints of Ecru and Ivory Buff). Neutral colours (chroma under neutral_chroma: steel, glass, white, black) and near-blacks (L* under dark_l: hair, char, the pupil) are reported, never off-palette. Calibrated 6 Nov on every asset (2,248 pictures, 8,804 main colours): the nearest Wada colour is a median ΔE 4 away, 99% within 9.9, the furthest 12.2; the book covers almost everything, so off_palette_de 10 flags the top 1% (at 14, nothing); at 10 most hits were near-black hair and char (the book has no warm near-black), hence dark_l. Since 6 Nov (Zafar) a colour that far off is a palette EXCEPTION (palette below), not a FLAG.

palette._about: One palette per item (Zafar, 6 Nov: "an item should have all of its main colors from within a palette that contains all those colors. If not, it needs redoing ... things that were just way off that aren't in there, raise it as an exception for me to decide"). The main colours are the k-means colours (colour above) with chroma at least neutral_chroma and L* at least dark_l (neutrals are the ground and exempt: the white marble #edecef is chroma 1.6; near-black hair and char have no Wada match), each at least main_share of the tinted pixels. FAIL when no single Wada combination (any of the book's 348, wada-colors.json) has a colour within combo_de (CIEDE2000, kL from colour) of every main colour. EXCEPTION (Zafar decides; on the block until he does) when a main colour is over exception_de from every Wada colour: it fits no combination at all. allow: globs Zafar has decided to keep, with his words and date (they pass the palette rule). Calibration: build/reports/art-review-strict-2026-11-06.md.

allow._about: glob: "Zafar, <date>: why". Empty until he decides the exceptions list.

wood._about: Walnut wherever there is wood (Zafar, 6 Nov; art bible section 2): lids, boards, handles, trays. FLAG (never a FAIL; meant for new art) a light oak or pine: the top band (a lid) of a lidded item by name (lid_names), or, on a picture whose name says wood (names), a main colour of at least share, in the light-wood band (CIE Lab hue degrees, L* l, chroma c). Walnut is Wada's Vandyke Brown (#4b3317, L* 23) to Brown (#7c4226, L* 35).

light._about: Light direction from the shading inside each material (pixels grouped by colour, lightness weighted down so a lit and a shaded side of one material stay one group), on the outer ring of the cut-out (convex shading; a bowl's inside lights the other way). angle: 90 = from above, 180 = from the left, 135 = upper left (the art bible). FAIL (Zafar, 6 Nov: "light and color should be failures ... on the block or in the pipeline for redoing") when the light is clear (strength over min_strength L* units) and comes from outside the allowed arc (the brightest quadrant is reported, not judged: a diagonal rolling pin's lower right was brightest under an upper-left light). People are skipped (skip: hair, jeans and faces are albedo, not light; the faces are a locked style, s17-fonts-review). A round piece (a bowl, pan or glass from above: the largest circle inside it covers over concave_round of its area) reading from the lower right (concave_arc) is the bible's light on a concave inside, so it is not flagged (a round convex piece from above lit wrongly is missed: a known limit). Calibrated on assets/cook/items (6 Nov): at 6 every top-down pan read 'lower right'.

halo._about: A near-white band just inside the alpha edge (outer edge_px of the solid piece) against the band behind it (inner_from..inner_to px): FLAG when the edge band is mostly near-white and much whiter than the band behind it. Calibrated 6 Nov: at 0.3 the six hits were steel rims, a hob's trim, a bubble and a wipe's crimped edge (true edges, not glows); 0.4 keeps a real halo (the test's is 100%).

shadow._about: A baked shadow: dark, low-chroma pixels below the object's body, either soft alpha (kept haze) or a solid dark skirt wider than the body above it. Soft pixels count only below the filled piece in their column and only where they show on a light ground (alpha x (1 - L*/100) at least shows), so clear glass's faint dark wall is not a shadow. FAIL: code draws the contact shadow (art bible section 2). Calibrated 6 Nov on every asset: 1 true shadow (scene/bowl-back.png); the two clinic glass belts were false until 'shows'.

opaque._about: Fable, 6 Nov: pan-pour's opaque crescent passed the soft and skirt tests. Per column: the opaque, neutral (chroma under dark_c) run at the bottom edge that grows lighter going down (by rise L* over the run, with up to tol L* of noise per pixel; at least min_run px or min_run_h of the height, at most max_run of it) from a contact line darker than the shadow's dark_l and gap L* darker than the body's next `above` opaque pixels. FAIL when such columns run unbroken across span of the width at an average depth px per column of the width; FLAG from flag_span. Calibrated on every asset (6 Nov): pan-pour 0.40 / 9.8 and the clinic sheets' toothbrushes 0.41-0.43 / 4-5 (true shadows), the parked chai cup and foot bath 0.22-0.29 (true); glass jar bases (shelf-spi-11, shelf-veg-14) 0.16-0.19 at depth about 1 (a glass base, not a shadow); dark pans, the black tea jar and top-down pans under 0.03.

faint._about: A faint soft shadow (a FLAG, never a FAIL): the soft-alpha test with a warm tint allowed (chroma under dark_c: a honey jar's shadow takes the honey's colour) at a smaller share of the bottom band. Fable, 6 Nov: clinic/items-v2/honey-jar.webp (0.033, 499 px). Calibrated 6 Nov: at 0.03, 84 pictures; looked at, the old cook props (tea tin, garlic, atto), the clinic's items-v2 (eye drops, plasters, thermometer) and the samosa folds keep a true faint grey under them.

house_look._about: House share as a FLAG (Fable, 6 Nov: what marks the stock pictures is strong colour with little of the house in it). Two rules. A rainbow, per picture: rainbow or more main colours outside the house family, each over loud_chroma and loud_share, their hues hue_apart degrees apart (the drop machine's RGBY tubes, the kite, the parked fever strip: 3 shipped of 1,653). A surface: in a batch whose median house share is at least surface_share, a picture under share at a mean chroma over chroma stands out (the well, the kite, the s09 ride's hen, bush and tree, the cook folder's tomatoes and chillies, the clinic's ice pack). Calibrated 6 Nov on every asset: the chai word-moment set flags nothing (its lowest, glass-we, is 0.21 at chroma 29; the tea cards 0.45-0.57 at 43-60 on a surface below 0.6); a single picture's house share flags 142 shipped at 0.4 / 45 (vegetables are rightly off the house), hence the surface. The onion (all Pompeian Red and Pale Burnt Lake, in the house) is not a colour finding: its stock look is shape and skin, a model's eye.

camera._about: Camera height proxy for round items (Fable, 6 Nov: the shelf's two batches differ in camera as much as in gloss): half-ellipses fitted across the width of the piece's body (after an opening of open x its size, which takes handles and spouts away) to its top and its bottom edge; rim = the top arc's height over the body's width (about 0 from the side, 1 straight down), read on files whose name holds one of names when both arcs fit (rms off by under max_err of the width, ratio under max_ratio) and agree within agree (a dome lid, a carton's gable or a bottle's foot do not). On a named surface the rims may span at most batch.camera_range. Measured on a copy at most side px. Calibrated 6 Nov: the chai shelf's bare jars 0.19, its v2 jars 0.26-0.45 (a range of 0.26: flagged); top-down pans, bowls and glasses 0.9-1.2; a pan with a long handle or a pour gives no reading (one arc).

gloss._about: A specular pixel: near-white (L* over spec_l, chroma under spec_c) and brighter than its 9 px neighbourhood by local_dl. gloss = their share of the solid pixels.

batch._about: Batch consistency (one surface, one run): per feature, the batch is split in two by 1-D 2-means; the smaller group is flagged when the gap between the groups is over min_gap (the feature's own units) and over sep times the spread inside the groups. A batch under min_items is not judged. The odd group is at most max_odd of the batch (a feature may set its own). The lid is the top lid_band of the piece; lids are compared by CIEDE2000 (lid_de), on a named surface or --batch only unless lid_in_folders (a folder holds bowls and jars; one shelf holds one lid family). A folder (not one surface) flags only a single odd one out, never a split (folder_odd_only): calibrated 6 Nov, folder splits were mostly one item's states (a pan empty and full), 400 flags of noise.

gloss.label: gloss (share of hard white specular pixels)

chroma.label: saturation (mean chroma of the solid pixels)

spec_x.label: specular position (across the piece, -1 left to +1 right)

halo.label: edge whiteness (share of near-white pixels on the outer edge)

soft.label: soft alpha (share of see-through pixels: glass and edge treatment)

batches._about: Named batches: the pictures that stand on one surface together (one shelf, one worktop), judged as one batch in a --scan as well as their folder. Globs from the repo root.

sizes._about: Proportion (Zafar, 6 Nov: token size steps, never true relative sizes): a size class per item, its target the share of the slot (canvas) height the piece fills: L 100%, M 90%, S 81% (equal ratio steps, each x0.9); tolerance under half a step, so the classes never overlap. min_css_px: the smallest piece is at least that many CSS px high on the smallest phone (at), so a slot there is at least min_css_px / S high (a layout rule for the game's code: artcolour.py --slot-css H checks a slot height). Items are matched by glob (first match wins); an item with no class is not measured.

block._about: The HOUSE LOOK lines artblock.py writes into every paste block (the colours themselves come from house above).
block.colours_note: Each picture's main colours come from ONE Wada combination, in lighter or darker tones (white, greys and near-black are free); a picture that mixes colours from different combinations, or has a colour the book lacks, is redone (Zafar, 6 Nov). Wood (lids, boards, handles, trays) is walnut, never light oak or pine.
block.edge_line: clean edges, no white halo, no rim light, no baked or drop shadow; light from the upper left.
block.sentence: Use the attached colour strip only as the palette (tones of these colours; never draw the strip, swatches or any text). Clean edges, no white halo, no baked shadow, light from the upper left.

shipped._about: Shipped by reference, not by folder (Fable, 6 Nov): a picture ships when a page, script, style or data file the game loads names it (pages), written out or built in code (a template literal's pattern, or its bare name quoted where its folder is named). lab: the lab pages, reported apart. exclude: data/asset-list.json is build/gen_assets.py's generation record (what was made, not what is shown: it names items/cook/onion-whole.png, which no page uses).

scan._about: What --scan skips: retina copies, any folder named in skip_dirs, and the second format of one picture (the webp is kept when a png or jpg of the same name sits beside it).
